recognize_zh: 左側 H&E 為高密度骨髓，含一個巨核細胞，漿細胞不易辨認；右側 CD138 顯示棕色膜狀陽性的漿細胞以鬆散小群與單個細胞散布整片，比 62847 那區的緊密叢集更分散，說明骨髓瘤浸潤分布不均（patchy）。
features: Side-by-side H&E and CD138 immunostain from a different area of the trephine
H&E: hypercellular marrow with mixed cells, a megakaryocyte at left, plasma cells not distinctly recognized
CD138: strong membranous staining of plasma cells in loose small clusters and singly dispersed cells
Plasma cells are numerous but interstitial and non-confluent, unlike tight sheets
CD138-negative residual hematopoietic cells between the clusters
describe_en: H&E section from another area of the bone marrow trephine shows hypercellular marrow with mixed hematopoietic elements and a megakaryocyte, in which plasma cells are not easily distinguished. The accompanying CD138 immunostain highlights numerous plasma cells with strong membranous staining arranged in loose small clusters and as single interstitial cells, without confluent sheets. Comparison with other areas demonstrates a variable, patchy distribution of the infiltrate, which is why the CD138 count should be estimated over the whole core. Findings are consistent with interstitial involvement by plasma cell myeloma.

ddx.vs: Reactive plasma cells are generally fewer, perivascular or single, and polytypic by kappa/lambda staining.
The distinction is quantitative: clonal plasma cell percentage (10% threshold) and myeloma-defining events, not morphology alone.
Discohesive plasmacytoid carcinoma cells can be CD138 positive but are cytokeratin, GATA3 and ER positive and kappa/lambda negative.
